sentences.text:
Author: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
Bench: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
 1
 Cmr, J.
 Crl. P.Nos.4291 of 2020 & Batch
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
 Crl. Petition Nos.4291, 4337, 4360 and 4367 of 2020
Common Order:

These Criminal Petitions under Section 482 Cr.P.C. are filed seeking quash of the respective F.I.Rs.
registered against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 272, 273, 328 of IPC and Section 58 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, "the FSS Act") etc.
2.

Since all these Criminal Petitions are filed seeking quash of the proceedings relating to similar nature of offences based on identical facts, these Criminal Petitions are heard together and they are being disposed of by this Common Order.

3. The petitioners sought quash of the criminal proceedings initiated against them on the ground that "tobacco" does not fall within the definition of "food" as defined in Section 3(i)(j) of the FSS Act.
Therefore, no offence under the said enactment is made out.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would also submit that these matters are squarely covered by the earlier orders of this Court and the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners therein based on similar facts for the similar offences are already quashed by this Court.

Therefore, they would submit that the petitioners, who are similarly placed, are also entitled for quash of the F.I.Rs.
registered against them in all these Criminal Petitions.

CMR, J.
Crl. P.Nos.4291 of 2020 & Batch 5.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor also fairly conceded that these are covered matters and criminal proceedings initiated against the other persons were quashed by this Court in the earlier orders passed by this Court.

8. Therefore, all these Criminal Petitions are allowed and the respective F.I.Rs. registered against these petitioners in all these Criminal Petitions are hereby quashed.
